items.text: The delay was largely ___ to a shortage of qualified staff.
options: blamed
caused
attributed
resulted

ok.de: Bei Ursachen entscheidet die Präposition: attributed to · blamed on · caused by · resulted from.
ok.en: With causes, the preposition decides: attributed to · blamed on · caused by · resulted from.

wrong.de: blame braucht „on“: The delay was blamed on a shortage …
wrong.en: blame takes "on": The delay was blamed on a shortage …

wrong.de: Im Passiv folgt „by“: was caused by, nicht „to“.
wrong.en: The passive takes "by": was caused by, not "to".

wrong.de: result hat kein Passiv: The delay resulted from a shortage …
wrong.en: result has no passive: The delay resulted from a shortage …

items.text: We lost the tender, but nobody is ready to ___ up hope just yet.
options: take
give
let
put

ok.de: Teilchen „up“ allein sagt wenig; erst das Verb macht die Bedeutung. Lern die ganze Wendung: give up hope.
ok.en: The particle "up" says little on its own; the verb carries the meaning. Learn the whole phrase: give up hope.

wrong.de: take up = mit etwas anfangen (take up a hobby).
wrong.en: take up = start something (take up a hobby).

wrong.de: let up = nachlassen; ohne Objekt (The rain let up).
wrong.en: let up = become weaker; no object (The rain let up).

wrong.de: put up = aufhängen, aufbauen; put up with = ertragen.
wrong.en: put up = hang or build; put up with = tolerate.

items.text: Our sales figures for Q3 are ___ better than we expected.
options: highly
strongly
heavily
considerably

ok.de: Komparative werden mit much/far/considerably verstärkt, nicht mit very oder strongly.
ok.en: Comparatives are intensified with much/far/considerably, not very or strongly.

wrong.de: highly steht vor Grundformen (highly effective), nie vor „better“.
wrong.en: highly goes with base adjectives (highly effective), never with "better".

wrong.de: „stark besser“ ist Deutsch gedacht; strongly passt zu Verben (strongly recommend).
wrong.en: "Strongly better" is a German pattern; strongly goes with verbs (strongly recommend).

wrong.de: heavily passt zu Menge oder Last (heavily invested), nicht zu Vergleichen.
wrong.en: heavily goes with amount or weight (heavily invested), not comparisons.

items.text: Hardly ___ we signed the contract when the client asked for changes.

ok.de: Hardly … when: Vorzeitigkeit, also Past Perfect, und nach „Hardly“ steht das Hilfsverb vor dem Subjekt.
ok.en: Hardly … when shows the earlier event, so past perfect, and after "Hardly" the auxiliary comes before the subject.

items.text: The more data we collect, ___ harder it becomes to see what really matters.

ok.de: Je … desto: the + Komparativ in beiden Satzhälften.
ok.en: The more … the more: the + comparative in both halves.

items.text: The supplier, ___ contract expires in May, has just raised its prices.

ok.de: Besitz im Relativsatz: whose (dessen/deren). who's = who is.
ok.en: Possession in a relative clause: whose. who's = who is.

items.text: The response to our new pricing model has been ___ positive.

ok.de: Vor einem Adjektiv (positive) steht ein Adverb: overwhelm → overwhelming → overwhelmingly.
ok.en: An adverb comes before an adjective (positive): overwhelm → overwhelming → overwhelmingly.

items.text: Due to ___ demand, we will repeat the webinar next week.

ok.de: Vor dem Nomen „demand“ steht ein Adjektiv; un- + precedent + -ed = noch nie dagewesen.
ok.en: An adjective comes before the noun "demand"; un- + precedent + -ed = never seen before.

items.text: The board has asked for a study on the ___ of the new pricing model.

ok.de: Nach „the … of“ steht ein Nomen; aus -ible/-able wird -ibility/-ability.
ok.en: A noun follows "the … of"; -ible/-able becomes -ibility/-ability.

items.lead: People say the company is planning to move its headquarters.

ok.de: Berichtspassiv: Subjekt + is said + to-Infinitiv; laufende Handlung: to be + -ing.
ok.en: Reporting passive: subject + is said + to-infinitive; ongoing action: to be + -ing.

wrong.de: „It is said that …“ braucht „It“ am Satzanfang. Nach „The company“ geht nur: is said to be.
wrong.en: "It is said that …" needs "It" at the start. After "The company" only "is said to be" works.

items.lead: I regret not checking the figures before the meeting.

ok.de: Bedauern über die Vergangenheit: wish + Past Perfect.
ok.en: Regret about the past: wish + past perfect.

wrong.de: Deutsch „hätte … gemacht“ verleitet zu would have. Nach wish steht für die Vergangenheit had + 3. Form.
wrong.en: German "hätte … gemacht" suggests would have. After wish, the past takes had + past participle.

items.lead: The project was delayed because the supplier did not deliver on time.
traps: due to the failure of the supplier

ok.de: Nominalstil: did not deliver → failure to deliver; der Grund steht nach due to/owing to.
ok.en: Nominal style: did not deliver → failure to deliver; the reason follows due to/owing to.

wrong.de: Sieben Wörter: zu lang. Mit dem s-Genitiv passt es in 3–6 Wörter.
wrong.en: Seven words: too long. The possessive 's fits into 3–6 words.

items.text: I'm really looking forward to hear from you.

ok.de: „to“ ist hier eine Präposition (look forward to sth); danach steht -ing.
ok.en: Here "to" is a preposition (look forward to sth), so -ing follows.

items.text: The client asked me where do we store the backups.

ok.de: Indirekte Frage: kein do, Wortstellung wie im Aussagesatz (where we store).
ok.en: Indirect question: no do, statement word order (where we store).

items.text: Had we known about the outage, we would have informed our customers.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: „Had we known …“ ist die förmliche Inversion von „If we had known …“.
ok.en: No mistake: "Had we known …" is the formal inversion of "If we had known …".

means.de: Wir haben unterwegs angehalten, um Kaffee zu holen.
means.en: We paused the trip in order to get coffee.

means.de: Wir holen dort keinen Kaffee mehr.
means.en: We no longer get coffee there.

transfer.text: Please stop ___ me reminders; I've already paid.

items.sa: On the way to the client, we stopped to get coffee.
items.sb: We stopped getting coffee from that café last year.

ok.de: stop + to = anhalten, UM etwas zu tun · stop + -ing = mit etwas aufhören.
ok.en: stop + to = pause in order to do sth · stop + -ing = no longer do sth.

means.de: Ich habe daran gedacht und ihn dann geschickt.
means.en: I didn't forget, so I sent it.

means.de: Ich erinnere mich, dass ich ihn geschickt habe.
means.en: I have a memory of sending it.

means.de: Ich muss noch daran denken, ihn zu schicken.
means.en: I still have to remember to send it.

transfer.text: Did you remember ___ the office last night?

items.sa: I remembered to send the contract.

ok.de: remember + to = an eine Aufgabe denken (danach) · remember + -ing = sich an Erlebtes erinnern (davor).
ok.en: remember + to = not forget a task (it comes after) · remember + -ing = recall sth you did (it came before).

transfer.text: It's optional: you ___ attend the Friday call.

items.sa: You mustn't share your login details.
items.sb: You don't have to share your screen.

ok.de: mustn't = verboten · don't have to = nicht nötig. Deutsch „muss nicht“ ist don't have to.
ok.en: mustn't = not allowed · don't have to = not necessary. German "muss nicht" is don't have to.

right.ex: We worked all weekend to meet the deadline.
If we miss the deadline, the bank will reject the application.
The client agreed to extend the deadline by a week.
Let's set a realistic deadline for the first draft.

note.de: make the deadline = es rechtzeitig schaffen (US, locker) – auch richtig, wird aber nicht abgefragt.
note.en: make the deadline = manage it in time (US, informal) – also correct, not tested here.

ok.de: Zu deadline gehören meet/miss/extend/set. „Einhalten“ ist hier meet.
ok.en: deadline goes with meet/miss/extend/set. German "einhalten" is meet here.

wrong.de: „Frist einhalten“ ist nicht hold: Man sagt meet a deadline.
wrong.en: German "einhalten" is not hold: you meet a deadline.

wrong.de: keep a deadline ist eine Lehnübersetzung; üblich ist meet.
wrong.en: "Keep a deadline" is a translation from German; say meet.

wrong.de: fulfill passt zu requirements oder obligations, nicht zu deadline.
wrong.en: fulfill goes with requirements or obligations, not deadlines.

right.ex: We can't afford to take that risk right now.
Companies that skip updates run the risk of a breach.
Outdated software poses a serious risk to your data.
Two-factor login reduces the risk of a breach.

note.de: carry a risk = ein Risiko mit sich bringen – auch richtig.
note.en: carry a risk = involve a risk – also correct.

ok.de: take/run = selbst eingehen · pose = für andere darstellen · reduce = verringern.
ok.en: take/run = accept a risk yourself · pose = be a risk to others · reduce = make smaller.

wrong.de: „ein Risiko eingehen“ ist take a risk, nicht go.
wrong.en: German "eingehen" is take here, not go.

wrong.de: make a risk gibt es nicht; ein Risiko schafft man mit create oder pose.
wrong.en: "Make a risk" doesn't exist; use create or pose.

wrong.de: do passt nicht zu risk.
wrong.en: do does not go with risk.

wrong.de: hold a risk ist kein Englisch; gemeint ist meist carry oder pose.
wrong.en: "Hold a risk" is not English; you probably mean carry or pose.

right.ex: We hold a team meeting every Monday morning.
Who's going to chair the meeting tomorrow?
Can we schedule a meeting for Thursday afternoon?
Twelve people attended the meeting in person.

ok.de: Meeting-Verben: hold/chair/schedule/attend. Deutsch „machen/besuchen“ führt in die Irre.
ok.en: Meeting verbs: hold/chair/schedule/attend. German "machen/besuchen" misleads.

wrong.de: „ein Meeting machen“ ist nicht make a meeting; man hält es ab: hold.
wrong.en: German "ein Meeting machen" is hold a meeting, not make.

wrong.de: „ein Meeting besuchen“ heißt attend a meeting.
wrong.en: German "besuchen" is attend here, not visit.

wrong.de: give a meeting gibt es nicht; give passt zu presentation oder talk.
wrong.en: "Give a meeting" doesn't exist; give goes with presentation or talk.

ctx.en: Reply to a new key account

items.text: We got your email and we'll get back to you soon.

why.de: have gotten ist US-korrekt, aber locker; formell: have received.
why.en: have gotten is correct US English but casual; formal: have received.

segs.span: we'll get back to you soon
accept: will get back to you shortly
choices: will get back at you soon
will come back to you soon

why.de: get back AT sb = sich rächen; come back to you ist eine Lehnübersetzung von „sich melden“.
why.en: get back AT sb = take revenge; come back to you is a translation of German "sich melden".

answers: We have received your email and will respond shortly.
We have received your email and will be in touch shortly.
We received your email and will respond shortly.

ok.de: Formell: vollständige Formen statt Kurzformen, received statt got, shortly statt soon.
ok.en: Formal: full forms instead of contractions, received instead of got, shortly instead of soon.

ctx.de: Verhandlung mit einem Lieferanten, den du behalten willst
ctx.en: Negotiation with a supplier you want to keep

items.text: Your offer is too expensive for us.

accept: is a little above our budget
might be a bit above our budget
seems to be slightly above our budget

why.de: Diplomatisch: Problem auf das eigene Budget verlagern und abschwächen (slightly, a bit, might).
why.en: Diplomatic: move the problem to your own budget and soften it (slightly, a bit, might).

answers: Your offer is slightly above our budget.
Your offer might be a bit above our budget.
Your offer is a little above our budget.

ok.de: Englische Geschäftssprache schwächt Kritik ab; deutsche Direktheit wirkt schroff (f25).
ok.en: Business English softens criticism; German directness sounds blunt (f25).

items.text: We need to talk about the problems with the rollout.

why.de: discuss hat ein direktes Objekt: discuss sth, nie discuss about.
why.en: discuss takes a direct object: discuss sth, never discuss about.

why.de: „Problematik“ ist nicht problematics; formell: issues regarding/concerning.
why.en: German "Problematik" is not problematics; formal: issues regarding/concerning.

answers: We need to discuss the issues regarding the rollout.
We need to discuss the issues with the rollout.
We need to discuss the issues concerning the rollout.

ok.de: Formell: ein Verb statt Verb + Präposition (discuss) und neutralere Nomen (issues statt problems).
ok.en: Formal: one verb instead of verb + preposition (discuss) and more neutral nouns (issues, not problems).

items.a: We postponed the launch because the tests had failed.
answers: The failure of the tests led to the postponement of the launch.
The failure of the tests resulted in the postponement of the launch.
The failure of the tests led to the launch being postponed.
The failure of the tests forced us to postpone the launch.
The failure of the tests made us postpone the launch.
options: The failure of the tests was caused by the postponement of the launch.
The failure of the tests led to the postponement of the launch.
The failure of the tests happened despite the postponement of the launch.
The failure of the tests will lead to the postponement of the launch.

ok.de: Nominalstil: failed → the failure of, postponed → the postponement of; verbunden mit led to/resulted in.
ok.en: Nominal style: failed → the failure of, postponed → the postponement of; linked with led to/resulted in.

wrong.opt: The failure of the tests was caused by the postponement of the launch.
wrong.de: Ursache und Wirkung vertauscht.
wrong.en: Cause and effect are reversed.

wrong.opt: The failure of the tests happened despite the postponement of the launch.
wrong.de: despite = trotz: Gegensatz statt Grund.
wrong.en: despite = contrast, not cause.

wrong.opt: The failure of the tests will lead to the postponement of the launch.
wrong.de: will = Zukunft; das Original ist abgeschlossen.
wrong.en: will = future; the original is finished.

items.a: We only noticed the gap after the audit.
answers: Only after the audit did we notice the gap.
options: Only after the audit we noticed the gap.
Only after we noticed the gap did the audit start.
Only the audit noticed the gap afterwards.
Only after the audit did we notice the gap.

ok.de: Only after/Only when + Satzteil am Anfang: danach Hilfsverb vor Subjekt (did we notice).
ok.en: Only after/Only when + phrase at the start: then auxiliary before subject (did we notice).

wrong.opt: Only after the audit we noticed the gap.
wrong.de: Bedeutung stimmt, aber nach „Only after + Zeitangabe“ fehlt die Inversion.
wrong.en: Meaning is right, but "Only after + time" needs inversion.

wrong.opt: Only after we noticed the gap did the audit start.
wrong.de: Reihenfolge vertauscht: hier käme die Lücke vor dem Audit.
wrong.en: Order reversed: here the gap comes before the audit.

wrong.opt: Only the audit noticed the gap afterwards.
wrong.de: Neues Subjekt: Das Audit bemerkt etwas, nicht wir.
wrong.en: New subject: the audit notices, not we.

items.a: The client said it was our fault that the data was lost.
answers: The client blamed us for the loss of the data.
The client blamed us for the data loss.
The client blamed us for losing the data.
The client blamed the loss of the data on us.
The client blamed the data loss on us.
options: The client blamed us for the loss of the data.
The client blamed itself for losing the data.
The client blamed us of losing the data.
The client blamed the lost data for us.

ok.de: blame hat zwei Muster: blame sb for sth · blame sth on sb.
ok.en: blame has two patterns: blame sb for sth · blame sth on sb.

wrong.opt: The client blamed itself for losing the data.
wrong.de: itself = der Kunde selbst: Bedeutung geändert.
wrong.en: itself = the client: the meaning changes.

wrong.opt: The client blamed us of losing the data.
wrong.de: blame sb FOR sth, nicht „of“ (Deutsch: beschuldigen + Genitiv).
wrong.en: blame sb FOR sth, not "of".

wrong.opt: The client blamed the lost data for us.
wrong.de: Es heißt blame sth ON sb; „for us“ ergibt keinen Sinn.
wrong.en: It is blame sth ON sb; "for us" makes no sense.
